statement: When the application declares a CorsConfigurationSource (the bean of its own stack's interface; Spring MVC's own HandlerMappingIntrospector is not a declaration) and registers no CorsFilter or CorsWebFilter of its own, the starter registers a CORS filter immediately before the pipeline's on Spring MVC and WebFlux. A preflight (OPTIONS with Origin and Access-Control-Request-Method) is then answered by that filter and is not decided: no policy, rate limit, blacklist, audit, decision event or metric sees it. An OPTIONS that is no preflight is decided as before; a request that is not a preflight is decided as before, and a refusal carries the CORS headers; an origin the source does not allow is refused by the filter before the pipeline. Without the bean nothing is registered and a preflight is decided as http:OPTIONS for an anonymous caller.
guards: spring-boot:CorsWiringTest#Spring MVC with a source answers a preflight before the pipeline and decides everything else
spring-boot:CorsWiringTest#Spring MVC without a source decides a preflight as before and registers no CORS filter
spring-boot:CorsWiringTest#Spring MVC with two sources fails startup and says to declare a CorsFilter
spring-boot:CorsWiringTest#a gateway host gets no CORS filter of the starter, with or without a source
spring-boot:CorsWiringTest#Spring MVC leaves the application's own CorsFilter alone
spring-boot:CorsWiringTest#WebFlux with a source answers a preflight before the pipeline and decides everything else
